summary: Describes how to carry MPEG-4 audio and video streams in RTP packets without using the MPEG-4 Systems layer. It defines the payload formats so receivers can rebuild the media from packets. It was replaced by RFC 6416.

eli5.summary: To send a video over the Internet you cut it into small packages. This says how to pack and label those pieces for one popular video and sound format.

questions: how to stream mpeg-4 over rtp
subtitle: How to send MPEG-4 video and audio in real-time packets over the Internet

tldr.problem: MPEG-4 is an efficient way to encode video and audio, but the Internet's RTP (Real-Time Transport Protocol) format for streaming was designed for simpler codecs. Applications need a standard way to break MPEG-4 streams into RTP packets without complex MPEG-4 container layers.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines how to fragment MPEG-4 audio and video bitstreams directly into RTP packets, including rules for where to split the data, which RTP header fields to use, and how to configure endpoints via MIME types and SDP.
tldr.outcome: Videoconferencing and streaming applications like H.323, SIP, and RTSP can now carry MPEG-4 media efficiently, competing with simpler codecs. The RFC was later replaced by RFC 6416 with updates for newer MPEG-4 profiles.

today: RFC 3016 is an Internet Standard and was obsoleted by RFC 6416, which adds support for additional MPEG-4 Visual profiles and levels, refines fragmentation rules, and updates references to newer MPEG-4 specifications. While older streaming systems may still follow RFC 3016, modern MPEG-4 streaming typically uses the newer RFC.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The RTP Payload Format for MPEG-4 Audio/Visual Streams enables direct transport of MPEG-4 encoded video and audio over RTP without using the full MPEG-4 Systems container. MPEG-4 is a powerful standard that supports variable bitrates (from tens of kbps to several Mbps), high error resilience, and object-based coding.

This payload format is designed for systems that already have stream management built in: H.323 terminals use H.245 signaling, while SIP and RTSP rely on SDP (Session Description Protocol). By skipping MPEG-4 Systems overhead, applications get simpler, more efficient streaming while still leveraging MPEG-4's coding advantages.
sections.eli5: MPEG-4 video is like a detailed instruction book for rendering video. Instead of sending the whole book, you can send just the instructions one page at a time, page by page, to someone who already knows how to read them.

sections.title: MPEG-4 Visual RTP Packaging
sections.content:
MPEG-4 Visual bitstreams are mapped byte-aligned into RTP packets without adding extra header fields. The fragmentation rules are flexible but enforce minimum constraints to protect error resilience:

  • Configuration information (Visual Object Sequence Header, Visual Object Header, Video Object Layer Header) must come at the beginning of an RTP payload.
  • Different Video Object Planes (VOPs, the MPEG-4 term for frames) should be placed in different RTP packets so the RTP timestamp uniquely indicates each frame.
  • Headers must never be split across multiple RTP packets.
  • Multiple small VOPs may be concatenated in one packet to reduce overhead.
  • Video packets should fit within the path MTU (typically 1500 bytes for Ethernet).
sections.eli5: Break the video into logical chunks (frames), make sure the instruction headers stay together, and fit them into Internet packets so they don't get fragmented again.

sections.title: MPEG-4 Audio with LATM
sections.content:
MPEG-4 Audio must be formatted using LATM (Low-overhead MPEG-4 Audio Transport Multiplex), which provides multiplexing and configuration data with minimal overhead. An RTP packet contains one or more complete audioMuxElements (an LATM container for one or more audio frames).

The configuration data (StreamMuxConfig) may be sent in-band (repeated periodically in each packet) or out-of-band (once via SDP). For scalable audio streams (layered coding), each layer should use a different RTP payload type so routers can prioritize base layers over enhancement layers if bandwidth is scarce.

The RTP marker bit signals the end of an audioMuxElement, allowing applications to detect and recover from packet loss. The RTP timestamp indicates the sampling time of the first audio frame in the packet.
sections.eli5: Audio is sent in specially formatted blocks. If the network gets congested, important layers (like a voice) can be kept while dropping fancy enhancements (like surround sound).

sections.title: MIME Types and Session Setup
sections.content:
For MPEG-4 Visual, the MIME type is video/mp4v-es (Elementary Stream). Key parameters include:

  • profile-level-id: Decimal value indicating which MPEG-4 Visual profile and level the stream uses (e.g., 1 for Simple Profile Level 1).
  • config: Hexadecimal encoding of the configuration information, sent out-of-band via SDP or MIME parameters.
  • rate: RTP clock rate (default 90 kHz).

For MPEG-4 Audio, the MIME type is audio/mp4a-latm with parameters like profile-level-id, object (audio codec type), bitrate, cpresent (configuration in-band), and config. The audio clock rate defaults to 90 kHz but should match the actual audio sampling rate when possible (e.g., 48 kHz for DVD-quality audio).
sections.eli5: When you set up a call, you tell the other side what kind of MPEG-4 you're using and give them the decoder setup instructions.

sections.title: Security and Error Resilience
sections.content:
RTP packets carry compressed media and are subject to standard RTP security mechanisms: encryption provides confidentiality, and authentication prevents tampering. Because MPEG-4 Visual includes built-in error resilience tools (Header Extension Codes, resynchronization markers), careful fragmentation can allow a receiver to recover from some packet losses.

The fragmentation rules recommend mapping at most one video packet (the MPEG-4 Visual unit between resync markers) to each RTP packet when networks are lossy, so a single packet loss does not discard an entire frame's worth of data. On reliable networks or low-bitrate links, multiple video packets can be combined to reduce IP header overhead.

MPEG-4 does not transport executable content (Java applets or scripts) in this payload format, unlike full MPEG-4 Systems, so there is no risk of code injection attacks.
sections.eli5: MPEG-4 video already has tools to recover from lost packets. Use them wisely: on bad networks, send small pieces separately; on good networks, you can bundle them together to save space.
